<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cb40147e19a3af9ffbf0be7251ec09f50867b499` — the merge of head `f4b177f6c29fb39860ae7834ced27ca4114e2beb` into base `8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cb40147e19a3af9ffbf0be7251ec09f50867b499 && git checkout cb40147e19a3af9ffbf0be7251ec09f50867b499
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d f4b177f6c29fb39860ae7834ced27ca4114e2beb && git checkout -B drift-repro 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d && git merge --no-ff f4b177f6c29fb39860ae7834ced27ca4114e2beb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · L1-c · ACCEPT · head `f4b177f6` · 2026-11-22T06:24Z

Read: the diff at `f4b177f6` (merge-base `a5a5312f`, 9 files, +1022/-0) against `l1-review-checklist.md`; dispatch order `seat4/a4-F/order-35955-3b.md` (card item 6, 「清掉」, seat 1's claim 7064104023 scope); the precedent `os db orphans`; the engine and driver paths the delete rests on.

**Mechanical face (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36304`).** Draft, base `main`, `Part of #35955`, no closing keyword; changeset `@objectstack/cli` patch (the order's `minor` was graded down to `patch` under `Metadata-protocol: none`, as the body explains); `Clause-②: no` (oclif-discovered, nothing exported from `index.ts`). Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`. `Check Changeset` was pending at the first read and finished `success` (run 137119119815). Every check at `f4b177f6` is now 42 success and 17 skipped, with 0 failed.

**The delete set is exactly the family (checked on the code).**
- The read is the driver's `$startsWith: 'ui.list.'`, unscoped. The SQL arm is case-exact on every dialect (`packages/core/src/utils/text-match-sql.ts` `dialectTextMatchSql`): SQLite uses `GLOB` without `lower()` unless folding, Postgres and Oracle compare the plain column, MySQL uses `CAST(… AS BINARY)`, and MSSQL uses its case-exact collation. So `UI.LIST.account` and `ui.listx.account` are out, as the integration suite seeds and holds.
- Defence in depth: the export read-back (`exportedIds`) judges each key byte-exact with `isListPreferenceKey`. A folding driver would therefore refuse the run with `export_incomplete` rather than delete a stray row. The body's dot-dropped ablation shows exactly that refusal.
- Live writers: on `origin/main`, `ui.list` appears in UI source only in a comment naming "the retired server row" (`app-shell/src/views/listLayoutStore.ts:25`). `ui.record.<object>` (`RecordPreferencesProvider`) is a separate family and untouched.

**The delete itself.** `engine.delete(object, { where: { id }, context: { isSystem: true } })` is the precedent's own call (`db/orphans.ts:319`); a scalar `where.id` is the single-row delete. `sys_user_preference` carries the platform prefix, so `recycleBinTakesObject` keeps it out of the recycle bin. The delete is hard, and "the export is the only copy" (CLI text and docs) is true. The order is right: export written `0600` with `wx`, read back and checked, then deletes of only the exported ids, then a re-read judged by what is gone. Rows written after the export are counted `unlisted` and exit 1 without deletion.

**Gates and boot.** The confirmation gate sits before the boot and joins the family's `migrate-confirmation-exit` roster; the body's ablation turns that pin red. The dry run boots read-only (`deferSchemaDdl` + `readOnlyProbe`), and `--apply` takes the plain boot, as `os db orphans --delete` does. The no-auto-run pin has positive controls first.

**Changeset and docs (read sentence by sentence):** `.changeset/35955-migrate-list-preferences.md`, the `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` row and section, and the `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` note.
- Flags, exit codes, the `0600`/no-overwrite export, re-runnability and "never run for you" each match the code.
- "Upgrading from 18.6.0 or earlier" matches `@objectstack/cli` `18.6.0` on main, with the Console change (#36133) unreleased.
- `ui.record.<object>` is "still read", matching `RecordPreferencesProvider`.

**Noted, no action:**
- The new `cli.mdx` table row sits between `audit-side-copies` and `comment-parent-pair`; the neighbouring rows run alphabetically, so it belongs after `comment-parent-pair`. Cosmetic.
- The occupancy probe runs before the `--yes` gate, so `--apply --json` on a busy SQLite file answers `database_busy` rather than `confirmation_required`. Both exit 1 with nothing read.
- The body's local readings are spread across `edcf4e1b`, `d6d3bf8c` and `f4b177f6` (stated); the head's own check-runs are the gate evidence.
- Out of scope, already filed as #36331.
- Landing: this is a governed stored-data delete, so the maintainer lands it after the seat's contract record. `Part of #35955` keeps `pm:dispatched` on the card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f4b177f6c29fb39860ae7834ced27ca4114e2beb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: no `reviewFace` hit in the committed tree (no governed path, no published schema; reviewed at tier on the seat's stored-data-delete order) + packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/list-preferences.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/list-preference-sweep.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/list-preferences.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/list-preferences.no-auto-run.test.ts, packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read: the diff `origin/main...f4b177f6` (9 files, +1022/−0, merge base `a5a5312ff4`, the merge commit of PR 3a #36133), the card body and its 12 comments, the PR body, dev report 7075257646, L1-c record 7075313108, #24949 and its pin, and the cited code outside the diff (read, not reviewed). The head's check-runs: 42 success, 17 skipped, none red. The PR is a draft, `mergeable_state` clean.

1. **The delete set is the retired family and nothing beside it.**
   - The family's key. At `a5a5312f^`, `ListPreferencesProvider.tsx:125,129` writes `ui.list.` plus the object name and nothing else, and `:449` together with `ConsoleShell.tsx:430` loads every row under that prefix as list state. So the prefix was the family's own namespace, not a shared one.
   - Other preference families at the head: `ui.record.`, `ui.recent`, `ui.favorites`, `ui.app.last`, `ui.flow.palette.recents`. None starts with `ui.list.`. The related-tab widths of #35892 sit in the `ui.record.` row (`RelatedList.tsx:1521`).
   - The command issues two queries and no third: the family read (`readListPreferenceRows`: object `sys_user_preference`, `key` `$startsWith` `ui.list.`) and the by-id delete on the same object. No other table and no other settings row is named anywhere in the diff.
   - The read is case-exact and escaped on every SQL dialect (`packages/core/src/utils/text-match-sql.ts`: SQLite `GLOB` without `lower()`, Postgres and Oracle the plain column, MySQL a binary cast, MSSQL a binary collation). The SQL driver's `find` applies no default row cap, so the read is the whole family.
   - A second guard that does not depend on the driver: the ids to delete must each be in the export as read back from disk, and `exportedIds` admits a row only when `isListPreferenceKey` passes byte for byte. A driver that returned a stray row would end in `export_incomplete` with nothing deleted.
   - The delete: `engine.delete(object, { where: { id }, context: { isSystem: true } })`, one call per exported id, the call `db/orphans.ts` makes. A scalar `where.id` is the single-row path. No object declares a reference to `sys_user_preference`, so no cascade follows. The platform prefix keeps the object out of the recycle bin (`recycle-bin/capture.ts:85`), so the delete is hard and "the export is the only copy" is true.
2. **Scope by organization, user and kind.** Every organization and every user, on purpose: card item 6 (「所有人回到视图本来的样子」) and the maintainer's 「清掉」. The read is driver-level and unscoped; the delete runs as the system. The kind is the key prefix alone. The integration suite seeds two organizations and holds five survivors (`ui.record.account`, `ui.recent`, bare `ui.list`, `ui.listx.account`, `UI.LIST.account`).
3. **Safe by default.**
   - Default run: a dry run on the read-only boot (`deferSchemaDdl`, `readOnlyProbe`), counts per key, never a value.
   - `--apply` needs `--export`; the export is written `0600` with `wx`, read back and checked before the first delete.
   - Count before deleting: the plan and "Deleting N row(s)" print before the export and the first delete.
   - Confirmation: `--yes`, or one prompt on a terminal.
   - Non-zero exits: `export_required`, `export_exists`, `database_busy`, `confirmation_required`, the text face off a terminal, `boot_failed`, `no_engine`, `export_failed`, `export_incomplete`, `scan_failed`, and any row still stored after the deletes all exit 1.
   - Idempotent: a second run reads zero rows, writes no export and exits 0 (pinned).
   - Outcome judged by a re-read of the family, not by what a delete returned.
4. **The #24949 family rules hold.** The command is in the discovered population and carries its roster row (`--apply --export`, confirm `--yes`, writes `BOOT`). Its gate sits before the boot. Off a terminal without `--yes` it exits 1 and names `--yes`; under `--json` it answers `confirmation_required` with exit 1. A decline at the prompt exits 0, which is the pin's own control ("an operator's decline is a choice").
5. **Ordering with PR 3a: no live reader.** PR 3a is the merge base. At the head and at `origin/main` `99fbaa6d18`, `ui.list` appears in source only as a comment (`listLayoutStore.ts:25`). The Console change and this command are both unreleased (`@objectstack/cli` is `18.6.0`, and the two #35955 Console changesets are still pending), so "Upgrading from 18.6.0 or earlier" is right. A run against a Console older than 3a breaks no screen: a reader with no row is the state every new user starts in, and the older Console writes the rows again, which the docs and the exit-1 re-read both say.
6. **Pins and ablations, read against the code.**
   - The integration suite runs a real boot on real SQLite; its order pin intercepts `ObjectQL.prototype.delete` and proves the export is complete on disk at the first delete.
   - The no-auto-run pin has positive controls first (`serve.ts`'s dynamic import, and the command's own import of its plan).
   - Ablation 2 (trailing dot dropped, 4 of 8 red) matches the code: the two look-alike rows enter the read, the dry-run counts move, `exportedIds` refuses them, the order pin is never reached and the re-run case exits 1; the four refusal cases stop before the read and stay green.
   - Ablation 3 (non-terminal gate disabled) matches too: the text face falls through to `confirm()`, which answers false off a terminal, prints "Aborted" and exits 0.
   - Ablation 1 (the in-memory re-filter stayed green and was removed) is consistent with the case-exact read. I did not re-run any of them.
7. **Docs and changeset, sentence by sentence.** The `cli.mdx` row and section, the `upgrading.mdx` note and the changeset each match the code: flags, the `0600` no-overwrite export, exit codes, "reads every organization's rows", "never run for you", re-runnable. The PR body's "40 success, 15 skipped" predates the body edit that re-ran the PR-body guards; the head now reads 42 and 17.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli` patch is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: nothing a metadata author can write changes, and `none` takes patch (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). `Clause-②: no` is true by the rule in `contract-review.md`: the published surface is the package's `exports` map (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`), and the diff adds nothing to `packages/cli/src/index.ts`; the command is reached by oclif discovery only. It is not a narrowing: no declared capability is taken from any consumer, and the rows it deletes have no reader. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed. Precedent is mixed and consistent with this reading: #29615 (a new `os migrate` command) declared `no`; #25039 declared a widening for a new exported `ObjectQL` method.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Governed handling.** No path in the diff is on the governed register, so the queue guard does not hold this PR by path. It is held by the seat's order (claim 7073280272: a stored-data delete lands only by the maintainer's hand) and the PR body asks for that. It is treated as governed: draft, unarmed, unqueued. This record does not ready it.
- **`Security-touching: yes`.** The changed hunks teach tenant-isolation behaviour: an unscoped driver-level read of every organization's rows, deletes in the system context across organizations, and one export file holding rows of every organization. That scope is the ruled one and matches `os db orphans` and `os secret orphans`; the line is `yes` because the hunks state it, not because it is wrong.
- **`Rule-change-verified: none`.** No hunk changes what an agent may do without the maintainer, the order of work, or what goes to him. The diff touches no `.claude/**` path, so the line carries no landing weight here.
- **Dev deviations, each answered.**
  - Changeset `patch` where the order said `minor`: correct, see ②.
  - Two family pins outside the claimed file list: both go red by name until a new member is rostered; they deliver the claimed command only.
  - Local runs narrowed because the shared lock timed out: stated in the body; the head's own check-runs carry Test Core on all ten shards.
  - PR body written at `edcf4e1b`: since updated by the area for `f4b177f6` (record 7075287677); the body now describes the gate before the boot.
  - Model-free commit trailers and the AGENTS.md footer: within AGENTS.md.
  - First push before `overlap-check`: an empty branch, nothing to overlap.
- **`open_questions`: none.** `security_findings: none` agrees with this read. The out-of-scope item is filed as #36331.
- **SQL push-down check.** The command materialises every family row and deletes by id, one call per row. A reason is given for `--apply` and it holds: the export must hold each deleted row as stored, and the delete set must be exactly the exported ids, so a predicate delete would also remove rows written after the export. The dry run has no such reason; see N2.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the card (item 6 and 「清掉」), the #24949 family rules and the `os db orphans` precedent: the design holds. The command deletes what was ruled cleared, cannot delete a row it has not first written to disk and read back, and reports honestly when rows remain.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the terminal prompt is asked before the boot, so before the run has counted anything; the count prints after the answer and before the first delete. This is the family's shape (the pin: "most gates sit before the boot"; `security-catalog-overlays --apply`, which also deletes, among them) and it has a reason: a declined run then boots nothing, where a plain `--apply` boot would already have run its schema sync. `os db orphans` asks after showing its count. The docs say dry run first, and the prompt names the whole family. A later pass could add "run without --apply to see the count" to the question.
- N2 (nit) — the dry run reads whole rows, values included, to produce counts it could ask the database for (a projection of `id`, `key`, `user_id`, `organization_id`, or a grouped count). The values never leave the process. On a large deployment `--apply` also holds the whole family in memory and deletes row by row outside a transaction; a partial run is safe to repeat.
- N3 (nit) — `planListPreferenceSweep` counts a null `organization_id` or `user_id` as one organization or reader, so a deployment whose rows carry no organization reports "1 organization(s)".
- N4 (nit) — `--export` without `--apply` is accepted and unused, yet an existing file at that path refuses the dry run with `export_exists`.
- N5 (nit) — the no-auto-run pin reads import specifiers inside `packages/cli/src`; a caller that reached the command by its oclif id would not be seen. Same reach as the `db/orphans` pin it copies.
- N6 (nit) — the new `cli.mdx` table row sits before `comment-parent-pair`; cosmetic, already noted by L1-c.
